gap: No result ChatGPT got states that QNAP's $1,299 TS-h966TX is rated for the same 20 Gbps Thunderbolt networking as the $2,499 TVS-h674T (ChatGPT's usual pick), and that QNAP measured it at 2,252 MB/s write and 2,004 MB/s read on a directly connected M4 Pro MacBook Pro. The TVS-h674T page gives no measured Thunderbolt speed at all.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP TVS-h674T and TVS-h874T US pages, the cited store.qnap.com Thunderbolt 4 category page, the cited UGREEN support pages and the UGREEN blog. The QNAP store page (cited in the 2026-11-07 chat) already shows TS-h966TX-8G at $1,299 and TVS-h674T at $2,499, and the TVS-h674T page states the 20 Gbps maximum. So the two prices and the rating are partly covered. None of ChatGPT's results contained the TS-h966TX product page, which has the measured Mac figures (2,252 MB/s write, 2,004 MB/s read), and no rival puts the officially supported models in price order. Our current page already has the TS-h966TX AJA numbers but quotes a pre-order price.
decides: If the shopper wants hard-drive capacity with a direct Thunderbolt link that the maker supports and has measured on a Mac, the TS-h966TX at $1,299 beats the TVS-h674T at $2,499. Both are rated at the same 20 Gbps, and the TS-h966TX has the only QNAP-measured Mac result. The TVS-h674T only makes sense for the Core i5, 32 GB of RAM and 6 SATA bays. For the lowest price, the UGREEN DXP480T Plus at $849.99 is the cheapest officially supported model, but it holds NVMe drives only. The DXP6800 Pro at $1,099.99 is the cheapest supported model with hard-drive bays, though UGREEN publishes only reference speed ranges for it, not a measurement. ChatGPT's TerraMaster and Asustor suggestions, and the UGREEN Ultra and iDX models, either lack Mac support or lack documented direct-connect support.

findings.label: TerraMaster direct-connect requirements
findings.value: Needs a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 port or full-featured USB4 port on the computer and a Thunderbolt 3/4/5 certified cable. The help page names no models and gives no bandwidth figure

unsourced: TerraMaster F6-425 Pro price and bridge bandwidth: terra-master.com returned HTTP 429 twice, the datasheet PDF returned 403 and B&H returned 403. A search snippet said '10-20Gbps' but I didn't use it because I never opened that page.

Whether the UGREEN DXP6800 Ultra, DXP8800 Ultra and iDX6011 support Thunderbolt direct connection to a Mac: their product pages returned HTTP 429, and UGREEN's support article lists only the DXP480T Plus, DXP6800 Pro and DXP8800 Plus.
Measured Mac-over-Thunderbolt speeds for the DXP6800 Pro, DXP8800 Plus and TVS-h674T/h874T: none on the maker pages I opened, and I didn't search reviewers because of the call budget.
Amazon and B&H prices for any model: B&H returned 403, and I skipped Amazon to stay within budget.
